reader.requirement: At --std 85 a function-identifier's class, category, size and value are those its 1989 Intrinsic Function Module definition gives (the 42 functions ACOS..WHEN-COMPILED): alphanumeric functions are identifiers of the returned length (reference-modifiable), integer and numeric functions stand only in arithmetic expressions, a function outside the module is no 1985 function, and argument class/count follow each definition; the witness covers UPPER-CASE, MAX/MIN alphanumeric and integer, MOD, NUMVAL, REVERSE, RANDOM, MEAN, LENGTH.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > Edition.DialectLevel / RemovedIn: COBOL1502 refuses a function outside the edition's window; the 42 module functions carry IntroducedIn 85
ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002): a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands is refused at 85 (COBOL0900, §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4), admitted 2002+
DialectBehaviors.IsActive(IntegerDateFormBounded): the four integer-date functions are unbounded above at 85 (1989 module), bounded at 9999 from 2002
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(Edition.Year): an argument predicate is asked only at an edition whose rule states it

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a numeric/integer function is legal only inside an arithmetic expression (refused as MOVE/DISPLAY operand), functions later than the 1989 module are refused, and DATE-OF-INTEGER past year 9999 returns the unbounded form (100880705) where 2023 returns 0.

reader.notes: BindIntrinsicCore resolves each function to its signature (result category, argument rules) and gates it by the edition window, so at 85 only the 42 module functions bind and each takes its definition's class; ScreenIdentifierPlacement enforces the 85-only SR4 placement and the integer-date functions take the 1989 unbounded arm. Every probe matched the definition; the per-function value rules are their own catalog rows.

refuter.evidence: Read the 1989 module's 1.2, 2.1-2.4 (Table 1, argument types A/I/N/X, 'A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required, even though a particular reference may yield an integer value' at §1985:p.A-29) and the LENGTH, MAX, RANGE, SUM, MOD, FACTORIAL, NUMVAL, ORD definitions. Refusal half at --std 85, each refused COBOL1627 as the definition requires: MOD(FUNCTION SQRT(16) 3), FACTORIAL(FUNCTION NUMVAL("3")) (numeric function in an integer position), MOD(WD 3) with PIC 9V9, MOD(2.5 3), CHAR(PIC S9(6)V99), RANDOM(PIC 9V9), ANNUITY(0.1 2.5) (integer argument); LENGTH(123) and LENGTH(WI + 1) (A-48 AR1: nonnumeric literal or data item only); MAX("A" 1) and MAX(WA WI) (AR1 same class); RANGE/SUM/MEAN over alphanumeric; ORD(5) and ORD of a 3-character item (AR1). Receiving-operand bar (SR3a): INSPECT FUNCTION ... REPLACING COBOL1632, STRING INTO / ACCEPT / UNSTRING INTO a function parse-refused; INSPECT FUNCTION ... TALLYING admitted (+000002), UNSTRING FUNCTION sender admitted. Admit half (fok-002): UPPER-CASE and REVERSE of a numeric-edited item (class alphanumeric), MAX/MIN mixing alphabetic and alphanumeric (the Amendment 2 C314 exception) returning alphanumeric, LOWER-CASE of PIC A, LENGTH of a numeric item 8 and of SIGN SEPARATE 9, LENGTH(CURRENT-DATE)=21, MAX(1 2.5)=2.50 numeric, MOD(MAX(7 3) 4)=3 and MOD(SUM(WI 2) 4)=1 (integer functions in integer positions), FACTORIAL(INTEGER(3.7))=6, RANGE(3 9.5)=6.50, NUMVAL-C("$1,234.50" "$")=1234.50, MOD(-11 5)+REM(-11 5)=3, MEDIAN(5 1 3 2)=2.50, alphanumeric function reference-modified. Class c: empty '( )' refused COBOL0900, N".." argument refused, function subscript refused, LENGTH(.. PHYSICAL) refused COBOL0900 at 85; NUMVAL-C with a data item named ANYCASE (not reserved at 85) binds it as argument-2, and NUMVAL-C("Fr.12.50" "Fr.")=12.50 takes the 1989 content-rule arm. NUMVAL(numeric-edited) is refused; 1985 'alphanumeric data item' is the PICTURE category (cf. §1985 IV reference-modification GR2 wording), so the refusal is the defensible reading. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.4 GR1; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR3 'As a receiving operand of any statement'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4 'may be used only in an arithmetic expression'; --find located A-29 and A-48 AR1. Side observation, not this rule: the COBOL1627/COBOL0844 messages at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses (15.64.3 etc.) rather than the 1989 module.
